Warm hello colleagues,
The lead dispatcher sent an update on tag checks

I'm flagging this for everyone on the Companion Animal Travel Desk because the handoff details need to stay clean and customer-first. When a traveler arrives with a pet, we should slow down long enough to confirm the crate, paperwork, and any comfort notes before the move starts. That extra pause keeps us from sending mixed messages and helps the traveler feel looked after rather than rushed. If the desk ledger needs an update, make it right away so the next colleague sees the same story and can keep the service smooth. <<FACT F044>> Keep an eye on small hazards around the holding area, and speak up fast if anything looks off.

I also want us to stay consistent when a pet cabin assignment changes or a service note comes through late. <<FACT F031>> We can avoid confusion by repeating the core details in plain language and checking that the traveler understands the plan before we close the interaction. If Ines Patel or Caleb Clark comes through with Poppy, give them the same calm, steady attention you would want for your own pet. The goal is simple: fewer surprises, fewer follow-up calls, and a better experience for the people and animals relying on us.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
